articles.headline: Champions League talking points: What to make of the Man Utd mess
articles.description: Gab Marcotti, Sam Tighe, Beth Lindop and Mark Ogden weigh in on an extremely embarrassing night for Man United, plus all the other moments that mattered from Matchday 3.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグの注目点：マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの混乱をどう見るか
articles.descriptionJa: ガブ・マルコッティ、サム・タイグ、ベス・リンドップ、マーク・オグデンが、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドにとって極めて屈辱的な一夜と、マッチデー3のその他の重要な瞬間について議論します。
articles.body:
The UEFA Champions League enjoyed a wonderful Matchday 3 this week, with a feast of goals -- 74 across 18 games, a 4.1 per game average -- and plenty to talk about.

We got big wins for our No. 1 ranked Paris Saint-Germain (over No. 2 Barcelona), Real Madrid (over RB Leipzig), Liverpool (over Villarreal), Real Betis (over Feyenoord) and Aston Villa (over Viking FK) as all five teams remain a perfect 3-0-0 in the competition, and we got a seismic shocks as Como thumped Manchester United to put Michael Carrick's future in doubt. The other big game of the week saw Bayern Munich and Arsenal put on an entertaining 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena, with Bukayo Saka limping off early with an injury.

What to make of it all? ESPN FC writers Gab Marcotti, Sam Tighe, Mark Ogden and Beth Lindop are here to break down the action.

- Ogden, Marsden: PSG and Barcelona put on a show

- Olley: Star attackers might not be needed for Arsenal to win UCL

- Dawson: Man United were woeful, but it's not just on Carrick

Q1. Are PSG going to regret going this hard against Barcelona? They may have won the proverbial battle with a 4-2 home win in the league phase, but they paid the price as Ousmane Dembélé hobbled off after just 20 minutes, with Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both exiting with injuries on the hour mark. (Kvara, one of the best players in the world, has since been ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn ACL.) We enjoyed the game, but will Luis Enrique & Co. regret losing one of their stars this early in the campaign? And will this derail their hopes of a remarkable Champions League "three-peat" at the same time?

Ogden: I'm not on board with this argument. Players can be injured at any time and Kvaratskhelia, Dembele or Marquinhos could have suffered the same fate in Sunday's Ligue 1 game at Lyon. It's just an occupational hazard and, let's be honest, Luis Enrique has rested and rotated all of his big stars throughout this season.

I think he was right to unleash the big guns against because it was a rare opportunity for his best players to go up against a team capable of challenging them. PSG's top players will get much more from playing against Barcelona and Manchester City than Le Havre or Auxerre.

If PSG hold back their stars against the likes of Barça, then they're going to have a very boring and unchallenging season in France, so I'm all in on Luis Enrique's selection. And also because it gave us a box office game and showed us just how good the latter stages of the Champions League will be.

Lindop: I'm with Mark on this one. As much as the new format means league phase games aren't hugely significant, PSG vs Barcelona is always a marquee fixture and there's no guarantee that players wouldn't have sustained injuries at other points of the season. PSG have the unique luxury of regularly being able to rest players in domestic competition so that they're at their very best in the Champions League, and it's an approach that has paid divide

articles.headline: Senators fans booing Tkachuk reminiscent of previous unpleasant sports returns
articles.description: Brady Tkachuk isn't the first notable sports figure to be met with jeers by fans of his prior team.
articles.headlineJa: セナターズのファンによるトカチュクへのブーイングは、過去の不快な復帰劇を彷彿とさせる
articles.descriptionJa: ブレイディ・トカチュクは、以前所属していたチームのファンから野次を受けた著名なスポーツ選手として初めての人ではありません。
articles.body:
On Wednesday night, months of mixed emotions for Ottawa Senators fans came to a head as Brady Tkachuk made his first trip back to the Canadian Tire Centre as a member of the Florida Panthers.

The Senators drafted Tkachuk in 2018, and he made three All-Star teams with the franchise. After being swept in the first round by the Carolina Hurricanes this past season, however, Tkachuk asked to be traded from the team so he could join his brother Matthew Tkachuk in Florida.

Senators fans let him have it when he took the ice, showering him with boos.

Tkachuk isn't alone in hearing the boo-birds on coming back to his former club, but if we were to include every contentious homecoming in sports, this article would drag on longer than an awkward encounter with your ex. Instead, we'll just regale you with some of the most memorable ones.

Juan Soto in New York, 2025

Soto spent the 2024 season with the Yankees before landing a 15-year $765 million contract with the Mets in the 2024 offseason. What was Soto welcomed to as his first time to Yankee Stadium as a Met? A shower of boos.

On top of that, every time Soto took the field on defense, Yankee fans also turned their backs on the right fielder.

John Calipari in Lexington, 2025

Calipari spent a decade and a half leading the Kentucky Wildcats before trading blue for red and accepting the Arkansas Razorbacks job last spring. Kentucky went to the Final Four four times under Calipari -- capturing a national title in 2011-12 -- but finished in unceremonious fashion each of his past four seasons.

The reaction when Calipari walked onto the court in his return to Lexington? A chorus of boos.

James Harden in Philadelphia, 2023

Harden spent a season and a half with the Philadelphia 76ers before being traded to the LA Clippers in October 2023. He requested a trade during the 2023 offseason and later called 76ers president Daryl Morey a liar after not being traded initially.

Philadelphia fans welcomed him as only they could -- booing Harden heavily during introductions and every time he touched the ball. They also cheered during his missed shots.

LeBron James in Cleveland, 2010

James went from being hailed as a hero to jeered as a villain quicker than the writers of "Game of Thrones." 

The environment was nothing short of combative as James returned to Cleveland for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat. The feelings of betrayal, disappointment and vitriol directed at him were tangible in the arena -- and in the city as a whole.

LeBron hadn't just been the most popular sports figure in Cleveland, he was one of its own. So his departure for South Beach brought about a different level of anguish to the championship-starved city that had its hopes and dreams resting upon his shoulders.

The "kid from Akron" was showered with boos and obscenities from former fans. Some of them threw things (including beverages and a battery); others held signs featuring things such as "Quitness" and "Witnessed No Champi

articles.headline: Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper on absence due to arrests: 'No excuses'
articles.description: Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper, now off the exempt list following two arrests on domestic violence charges in June, said he holds himself accountable.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスのOLBジョナサン・クーパー、逮捕による欠場について：「言い訳はしない」
articles.descriptionJa: 6月に家庭内暴力の容疑で2度逮捕され、現在は免除リストから外れたブロンコスのOLBジョナサン・クーパーは、自分に責任があると考えていると述べました。
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, said Wednesday he had "no excuses'' and that he holds himself accountable.

Cooper had been on the commissioner exempt list since the start of the regular season, so he had been unable to practice with the team or play in any of the Broncos' first six games. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell removed Cooper from the exempt list Friday after Cooper's trial had been moved from November to March. Cooper returned to practice for the first time Wednesday.

While he declined to address specific questions about his case, Cooper was asked Wednesday what he would say to people, particularly female fans, as he returns to the field.

"Honestly ... that's hard, I feel like, relationships are difficult, [but] no excuses on my end,'' he said. "I do apologize for anybody's feelings, truthfully, because you have to be associated with me. I'm a grown man, I'm able to take things on the chin and I understand the concern, the awareness, how serious these matters are, the legal matters will take care of themselves.

"Nobody's perfect, but there's no excuses. And I do hold myself accountable and things are going to sort themselves out, I promise that.''

 

Cooper was in Douglas County (Colorado) court Oct. 12 for a motions hearing and had a March 2 trial scheduled in his case during that appearance. On Friday, when the NFL announced Cooper had been removed from the exempt list, the league said in a statement the review of Cooper's case "remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper's roster status.''

It means Cooper could still face league discipline at a later date under the NFL's personal conduct policy. The Broncos have a one-week roster exemption for Cooper, but the team would have to make a move this week to add him to the 53-player active roster to have him available to play in games, including Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.

The exempt list is designed to remove a player from participation in games and practices while potential violations of the NFL's personal conduct policy are reviewed. Cooper has been paid while on the list.

"The legal matters ... everything will sort itself out, that process is going to keep going on,'' Cooper said. "That will all get cleared up.''

Cooper faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, after he was arrested June 4 and again June 11 after incidents with his girlfriend. The felony charge stemmed from the first arrest after the results of a forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend by a nurse.

articles.headline: Packers' Josh Jacobs says he is trying to learn from 'mistake,' move forward
articles.description: Josh Jacobs, in his first comments since his arrest in May following an incident with a woman at his home, said he is trying to move forward from the "mistake."
articles.headlineJa: パッカーズのジョシュ・ジェイコブス、「間違い」から学び前進したいと語る
articles.descriptionJa: 自宅で女性とのトラブルにより5月に逮捕されて以来、初めてコメントしたジョシュ・ジェイコブスは、この「間違い」から乗り越えようとしていると述べました。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs, in his first comments since his arrest in May following an incident with a woman at his home, admitted Wednesday that he made a mistake but said he was never concerned that his career was over and did not think he would miss as many games as he did.

"I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation," Jacobs said, his voice quivering. "Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly. But with that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process.

"I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that's been around me, I'll let them do that. But for me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward."

Jacobs had been on the NFL commissioner exempt list since the start of the regular season, meaning he could not practice or play in the first six games. He could be around the team facility and work out there. The league removed him from the list Monday, although its investigation into violations of the personal conduct policy remains active. The six games he has missed will be credited toward any suspension that could be forthcoming, but as of now, Jacobs is cleared to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions.

"I think six games was a lot, honestly, but that's not really up to me to decide," Jacobs said. "I'm grateful to be playing, so that's not even something that I'm like arguing or petitioning with. I'm just happy to be back on the team."

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property resulting from the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and reached a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property.

"I would say obviously you never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me," Jacobs said. "I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what's important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. When they think of me, what are they going to say? Another thing that it showed me, man, was the people that were in my corner. A lot of people I didn't even know or even expect to be in my corner, they showed up. So that was huge for me. It just gave me more appreciation, more love honestly for this organization and this team."

The Packers have stood by Jacobs from the start and allowed him to participate in the entire offseason program and training camp.

articles.headline: Cornell Green, 5-time Pro Bowl DB on Cowboys' Doomsday Defense, dies at 86
articles.description: Cornell Green, who never missed a game in 13 seasons while playing for the Cowboys from 1962-74, died at age 86.
articles.headlineJa: カウボーイズの「ドゥームズデイ・ディフェンス」の一員で、プロボウルに5度選出されたDBのコーネル・グリーンが86歳で死去
articles.descriptionJa: 1962年から74年までカウボーイズでプレーし、13シーズンにわたり一度も試合を欠場することのなかったコーネル・グリーンが86歳で死去した。
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Cornell Green, a defensive back who never missed a game in his 13 seasons with the Dallas Cowboys and was part of their original Doomsday Defense, has died at age 86, the NFL team said Wednesday.

The team provided no details on the cause of his death.

Green didn't play football in college and instead was an NBA draft pick in 1962 before being invited to attend the Cowboys' training camp that year.

He made the Dallas roster and played in all 182 regular-season games from 1962-74, plus 15 playoff games. He was part of Cowboys' first Super Bowl championship during the 1971 season and later selected as part of their 25th anniversary team.

"Cornell was a true trailblazer having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All-Pro and NFL Super Bowl champion," the Cowboys said in a social media post. "Cornell remarkably never missed a game in 13 seasons, becoming one of the best and most dependable teammates to ever wear the star."

Green was selected to five Pro Bowls and was a first-team All-Pro selection by The Associated Press in 1966 and 1967. His 34 career interceptions are tied for fifth-most in team history.

Born in Oklahoma City, Green grew up in California, where he played basketball at El Cerrito High School, and also played football as a junior. He played two seasons at a community college in California before transferring to Utah State, where he is still the career leader with 1,067 rebounds and ranks sixth with the 1,890 points he scored over two seasons (1960-61 and 1961-62).

The Chicago Zephyrs, the NBA franchise that became the current-day Washington Wizards, drafted Green in the fifth round with the 37th pick overall.

But he instead went to the NFL, where he started three of 14 games as a rookie, and then 167 of 168 the rest of his career. He was a cornerback his first eight seasons and moved to safety his final five seasons.

After retiring as a player, Green spent time as a scout for the Cowboys and later the Denver Broncos.

articles.headline: Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy thriving in expanded role as Seahawks loom
articles.description: The Chiefs will likely need similar improved play -- or even better -- from Worthy in Sunday's showdown vs. Seattle.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークス戦を控え、役割を拡大したチーフスのWRザビエル・ワーシーが躍進
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のシアトルとの対戦において、チーフスはワーシーに対し、これまでと同様の向上したプレー、あるいはそれ以上の活躍を期待することになるだろう。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- When Chiefs receiver Xavier Worthy entered Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, he knew the team's offensive game plan was different for him.

"They told me all week it's going to be for me, and I've got to step up for the receiver room," Worthy said of the coaching staff following the Chiefs' Week 6 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. "Guys are down, so I did my job."

The proof was demonstrated in the Chiefs' opening possession. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes' first passing attempt was for Worthy. As the game progressed, the Chiefs' need for Worthy to have a strong performance increased. Tight end Travis Kelce, Mahomes' most reliable pass catcher, sustained a right ankle injury in the first quarter.

Mahomes responded by trusting Worthy -- and the receiver kept rewarding the Chiefs. In his best performance of the season, Worthy, a third-year player, finished Sunday's game with a game-high seven receptions for 73 yards. The Chiefs' offense needed Worthy's production, too, especially since it was Mahomes' first game this season without his top receivers: Tyquan Thornton, who was placed on injured reserve last week after suffering a dislocated left ankle, and Rashee Rice, who is recovering from a strained right hamstring.

Worthy on Wednesday compared getting targets early in Sunday's game that led to positive receptions when a basketball player swishes multiple shots in the first quarter.

"You hit five in a row [in basketball], it doesn't get any better than that," Worthy said, smiling. "It obviously built the confidence and led to a strong game."

The 5-0 Chiefs will likely need similar play -- or even a better performance -- from Worthy in this Sunday's showdown against the Seattle Seahawks (3-3), the NFL's defending champion.

For much of his career, Worthy has tried to become the speed threat many had hoped after he broke the record for the 40-yard dash at the 2024 NFL combine (4.21 seconds). He showed sizable improvement as a rookie, recording 638 receiving yards and nine total touchdowns. But last season was a disappointment. He sustained a significant right shoulder injury on opening night when he collided with Kelce while running a crossing route.

Coach Andy Reid acknowledged the Chiefs had to adjust the routes Worthy ran last season to better protect his shoulder. He finished with 532 receiving yards and one touchdown.

"People look at him because he's a little bit smaller and he's real fast, so they think of him as just a deep threat," Reid said of Worthy, who is listed at 5-foot-11 and 165 pounds. "We've always looked at him like he can run shallow crosses, deep crosses. He can do all that stuff and [is] very good at it. He's tough and he's smart, so you can move him around a lot in a lot of different spots."

articles.headline: Bucs QB Jalon Daniels swaps jerseys with idol, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers
articles.description: Following Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory, Jalon Daniels left with a keepsake from his idol, Aaron Rodgers.
articles.headlineJa: バッカニアーズのQBジャロン・ダニエルズ、憧れの存在であるスチールザーズのQBアーロン・ロジャースとユニフォームを交換
articles.descriptionJa: ピッツバーグが26-19の延長戦で勝利した後、ジャロン・ダニエルズは憧れのアーロン・ロジャースから記念品を受け取った。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- All last week, teammates of Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels urged him to do it.

"I was talking to the quarterbacks beforehand and they basically were just like, 'If you get the opportunity to ask him, you better ask him,'" Daniels told ESPN.

Fellow Buccaneers quarterback Brett Rypien told Daniels, "If you didn't ask him, I was going to ask for you," Daniels recalled.

They were talking about Daniels meeting his idol -- Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who on Sunday led Pittsburgh to a 26-19 come-from-behind overtime victory over the host Bucs -- and asking for a jersey.

"Last season, last go around for him. So, I had to ask before he got up out of here," Daniels said, referring to Rodgers' plans to retire following the 2026 campaign.

Daniels summoned the courage to do so and was met with a long embrace, which was captured on camera postgame and showed a tender side to Rodgers not often seen because of his intensity in games.

"I mean, it was kind of crazy," Daniels said. "So, just kind of ... without trying to completely ask that -- I don't want to be that guy -- and he was just like, 'I know exactly what you're getting at. I'll give you the jersey.' And then I'm like, 'All right man, thank you.'" The pair shook hands. Daniels then heard something he never imagined: The Super Bowl winner and future Pro Football Hall of Famer wanted his jersey too.

"[I] was about to walk away and he was like, 'Wait, hold on. Can I get yours?'" Daniels recalled Rodgers asking. "Now, that's kind of what caught me by surprise."

What Daniels didn't know was how much Rodgers knew of and respected his game from afar. The week prior, the 2026 undrafted free agent led the Bucs to a 24-16 primetime upset at the Dallas Cowboys. It was the Bucs' first victory of the season and just Daniels' second career start, which came unexpectedly after starter Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb in Week 3.

"I appreciate the respect," Rodgers said of Daniels on the CBS broadcast. "Super respectful guy. I like his game. I like the way he throws it. Obviously, super talented with his feet. I'm excited to see how he develops. Learning behind a guy who's played a long time like Baker is obviously going to be great for him."

Daniels was touched by the praise.

"I respect that, as well," he said. "It's not every day you hear that from a Hall of Famer."

Rodgers' ability to perform in high-pressure situations, make passes from different angles, get out of the pocket and throw off-platform were elements Daniels tried to bring to his own game as a six-year starter for Kansas -- after Daniels was initially supposed to redshirt. Daniels' career as a Buccaneer began in similar fashion by not hearing his name called at all during draft weekend and starting Bucs training camp fourth on the depth chart. He moved all the way up to No. 2 by beating out veteran Jake Browning -- who had previously started 10 career games for the Cincinnati Bengal

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim with 'nothing to say' about Man United on return to England
articles.description: Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ルベン・アモリム、イングランド復帰にあたりマン・ユナイテッドについては「何も言うことはない」と述べる
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜夜に行われるボーンマスでのACミランとのヨーロッパリーグの対戦を前に、ルベン・アモリムはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドについて「何も言うことはない」と強調した。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 14 months in charge, and was appointed by the Serie A side in June.

Amorim revealed he does not think he has changed as a person since his time with the Red Devils, but believes he has become better at his job.

"Overall, I think the important thing is that I'm here as AC Milan's manager," said Amorim, speaking at a press conference at the Vitality Stadium and quoted by Milan News.

"I have nothing to say about United. I can say that I loved the club and the atmosphere: what happened doesn't change that.

"Then I moved on, now I'm at AC Milan and I'm focused on this: at every big club, problems are always around the corner. I focus on ourselves and I don't think about the teams. My past at United doesn't matter; what I said when I signed there remains the same."

Amorim revealed Samuel Chukwueze is out with a hip problem, and Gonçalo Ramos has sustained a calf strain, and expects 19-year-old Alphadjo Cissè, who he believes has reached only "50 per cent of his potential" to feature in Thursday's line-up to face the Cherries.

"I have more experience as a coach, but I'm not a different person," Amorim added, reflecting on his spell with United.

"I understand football better, and that will help me deal with problems in the future. I think I'm the same person, just a little more experienced in some things."

The man who replaced Amorim at United, Michael Carrick, has seen his position come under serious pressure in recent weeks as the club have endured a torrid start to the new season. 

His team were beaten 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' Como in Italy on Wednesday in a match that saw Carrick and Fernandes appear to trade barbs through their post-match comments to the travelling media.

- Dawson: Man United players were abysmal in Como, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

articles.headline: Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in Sunday's Clásico
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has warned that "not much" should be read into Madrid's dismantling of RB Leipzig ahead of Sunday's Clásico, but Jose Mourinho is surely starting to figure out who his best XI is.
articles.headlineJa: バルベルデとギュレルが、日曜日のクラシコでマドリードの鍵となる理由を示す
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペは、日曜日のクラシコを前にマドリードがRBライプツィヒを粉砕したことについて「あまり意味はない」と警告しているが、ジョゼ・モウリーニョは確実に自身のベストイレブンを絞り込み始めている。
articles.body:
MADRID -- What can Real Madrid take from their 4-1 win over RB Leipzig into Sunday's Clásico with Barcelona? If you believe Kylian Mbappé, not much.

"It's completely different," he told Movistar, speaking seconds after the final whistle in Wednesday's UEFA Champions League game at the Bernabéu. "We've only thought about tonight's game. The team hasn't thought about Sunday yet."

Still, watching Madrid dismantle Leipzig in the second half -- when goals from Arda Güler, Mbappé and Yan Diomande followed Bernardo Silva's first-half tap-in to ensure a comprehensive win -- it was impossible not let your mind drift towards the implications for Camp Nou.

Is Federico Valverde now Madrid's first-choice right-back, ahead of two specialists in Trent Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries? Will coach José Mourinho risk Güler in central midfield, or play it safe and shift him out to the wing? And is Diomande now certain to start, having followed his brilliant goal against Sevilla on Sunday with another, even better strike off the bench?

- As it happened: Como stun Man Utd, Real Madrid run riot over RB Leipzig

- United players were abysmal, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

- Watch El Clásico LIVE, 10/25, 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

"It's been 105 days that I've been here, it isn't many," Mourinho said post-match. "I need to get to know [the players], and the best place to do that is on the pitch, in competition."

Earlier this season, Mourinho had been insistent about Valverde's role. "He can play [at right-back], it's happened in the past, but for me, he's a central midfielder," the coach said in August.

Wednesday's performance, Valverde's second in a row at right-back, suggested otherwise. There were moments of discomfort, like when he was beaten early on by Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa. But after that, he barely put a foot wrong. Over 90 minutes, Valverde had the most touches (115) of any player on the pitch. He completed the second-most passes, after Dean Huijsen.

At one end, he created three chances, playing three key passes, including the cross from which Silva scored, after Güler's shot fell to him. At the other end, no player had more defensive interventions (12, to Huijsen's 11), which includes tackles, interceptions and clearances.

In other words: Valverde was everywhere. After a performance like this, it's hard to imagine him not staying at right-back against Barcelona.

The only player who rivalled Valverde for influence in Madrid's play was Güler. In just the last week, in games against AS Roma, Sevilla and Leipzig -- all respectable opposition -- Güler has contributed two goals and two assists. Against Leipzig, Güler just beat Valverde to the most passes played into the final third, with 27 to Valverde's 26.

He played here on the right wing, and the only question on Sunday is whether Güler stays there, or returns to the centre, in a more attacking, ambitious formation, which might go against Mourinho's instincts.

Arsenal have joined the race to sign Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, while Crystal Palace duo Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are on the radar of Manchester United ahead of the January transfer window. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Arsenal have joined the race to sign Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, according to The Sun. The 22-year-old has caught the eye of Europe's top clubs following his UEFA Champions League hat trick against Internazionale, as Mikel Arteta looks to bolster his attacking options. The Gunners are also in the final stages of negotiations with midfielder Declan Rice over a new long-term contract, according to Fabrizio Romano.

- Manchester United are monitoring Crystal Palace duo Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta ahead of the January transfer window, TEAMtalk reports. Both players face uncertain contract situations, with Mateta's deal expiring in 2027 and while Sarr has a deal until 2029, he is weighing up a new offer from Palace amid interest. United are also set to bring in a left back next summer, with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert being scouted, according to iNews.

Despite heavy interest from Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich, a fresh contract for the 19-year-old through 2030 has secured his long-term future at Camp Nou. Espart is a natural midfielder but has been deployed as a full back on either side this season as he made the breakthrough into the first XI.

- Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez is set to leave the club at the end of the season, according to The Daily Mail. Last week, Martinez, 28, criticized the United hierarchy over their recent record in the transfer market and later apologized, but the Argentina international's future has now been cast into serious doubt. 

- Tottenham Hotspur right back Pedro Porro would "seriously consider" a move to Barcelona or Real Madrid, reports Football Insider. Despite signing a contract extension until 2031, the 27-year-old is enticed by the prospect of competing for trophies and playing in the Champions League in Spain.

articles.headlineJa: 関係者：マーベリックス、ウォルター・クレイトン・Jr.と2ウェイ契約に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNの取材によると、マーベリックスは元ドラフト1巡目指名のウォルター・クレイトン・Jr.とNBAの2ウェイ契約を結ぶことで合意した。
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks have agreed on a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday.

Clayton was waived earlier this week by the Memphis Grizzlies ahead of the league's roster cut-down deadline. He is joining the Mavericks after clearing waivers.

Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr., Jock Landale, John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range.

Clayton, 23, was the No. 18 pick in the 2025 draft after helping Florida win its third national title. He was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player and was a consensus first-team All-American in 2025.

The Mavericks, still light on ball handlers despite the return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury, could use the depth Clayton provides in their backcourt.

The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Oct. 21

Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal

Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return.

Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season.

Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks

Sources: Warriors begin exploring trades for Porzingis

The Golden State Warriors have begun the process of looking for trades for center Kristaps Porzingis, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Porzingis remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has had him questioning his future with basketball.

If there isn't a breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from his career is possible, sources told Charania.
